Hi Lena —

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciate you walking us through the team goals. Quick recap of the key points I captured and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Pain points / goals we heard
- High per-token inference cost on current vendor during peak clinical throughput (ER triage use case).
- 95th percentile latency target < 250ms for short prompts (~200 tokens).
- Need predictable scaling and audit logs for compliance (SOC2 / PHI).
- Must support private deployment for the production environment; hosted is OK for dev testing.

Decision criteria you shared
1) Latency & throughput under peak burst
2) Cost per 1M tokens (incl. inference + egress)
3) Security controls (VPC, KMS, audit trail)
4) Ease of integration + SDK support for Python/Go
5) Vendor response on runbook & escalation SLA

Competitive landscape (as discussed)
- Current vendor: AcroAI — strong on accuracy but cost and scaling issues.
- Vendor B: OmniServe — good latency, weaker security controls.
- Redwood (us) — focused on production economics, private deployment option, detailed observability and fallbacks.

Proposed follow-ups / next week plan
- Redwood test plan: run a 48-hour throughput/latency test against a representative workload (we'll send config). (Action: Redwood — Marissa to own test plan)
- Price delta worksheet: we shared an MVP pricing model (attached MVP-pricing.xlsx). We'll update with NovaHealth-specific assumptions after test. (Action: Aditya)
- Security questionnaire & SOC2 evidence: we'll share the evidence bundle and scope for Private deployment. (Action: Aditya / Marcus)
- Technical Q: Are there any disallowed system prompts or policies we should sandbox during tests?

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-ask.pdf (overview + test ask), MVP-pricing.xlsx

If this looks right, can we lock the following:
- Test window: Wed 5/12 08:00–20:00 PT (48h)
- Decision checkpoint: Fri 5/14 10:00 PT (30 min)

Thanks — I'll wait for confirmation on the test window and any restricted prompt lists.

Best,

Hi all —

Thanks for the confirm, Lena. Quick technical plan and what we'll need from NovaHealth to make the bake-off deterministic: 

1) Workload capture: A 24–48 hour sample of anonymized request traces (timestamps, prompt lengths, endpoint used). If you can't share traces, we can review a distribution (percentiles) for sequence length and request concurrency.
2) Allowed/disallowed prompt rules: the list Lena referenced — we will ensure the test harness filters or masks those fields.
3) Test configuration (what we'll run)
   - Model variant: rwd-3b-opt (comparable to your baseline model)
   - Concurrency profile: burst to 200 concurrent requests, sustained 50 rps
   - Target latency SLO: p95 < 250ms for < 200 token prompts
   - Duration: 48 hours (we'll do a warm-up + two full cycles)

4) Metrics we'll capture and share (raw & aggregated): latency percentiles, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, error rates, KV cache hit rate, and cost per 1M tokens (estimated).

5) Follow-up tests: accuracy/regression test on a shared eval set (we can run same prompts through Redwood and current vendor and provide side-by-side outputs).

Attached is the test plan draft: redwood-test-plan.md — this includes the exact commands, container images, and infra we use for an apples-to-apples run. We'll also include a short script to mask sensitive fields prior to testing.

Questions for NovaHealth
- Who will own the anonymization step? (NovaHealth preferred)
- Can we get a short-lived IAM role/endpoint or allowlist IP range for the test traffic?

Proposed owner assignments
- Redwood (Marissa): test harness, metrics collection, shared results dashboard
- Redwood (Aditya): pricing update and line-item PDF for procurement
- NovaHealth (Lena / Evan): anonymized traces, procurement approval for the test window

I'll plan to spin up the harness on Wed morning pending procurement confirmation.

Best,
